endpoint_inventory.summary: Get a Site Collector agent installation command
endpoint_inventory.description:
Install command to install the Site Collector agent. The command is encoded in base64, necessitating a decoding step. This encoding ensures the command's integrity during transmission, maintaining its format and preventing alterations. For example, after you receive the response, you can decode the string using the command `base64 -d <<< "c3Vkb..............."`.
After decoding the command from base64 to its original string format, you'll have the necessary shell commands to install the Site Collector agent. The install command varies depending on the type of Site Collector agent as defined in the Site Collector template. The command sequence downloads and runs a script to configure the agent and passes in parameters (`deploymentHosts`, `templateIds`, and optionally `fetchStartDate` and `fetchHistoricalData`) that affect how the script configures the Site Collector agent.

Support package command to generate the support package of the Site Collector agent.  The command is encoded in base64, necessitating a decoding step. This encoding ensures the command's integrity during transmission, maintaining its format and preventing alterations. For example, after you receive the response, you can decode the string using the command 
`base64 -d <<< "c3Vkb..............."`
After decoding the command from base64 to its original string format, you'll have the necessary shell commands to generate the support package of the Site Collector agent. The support package command varies depending on the type of Site Collector agent as defined in the Site Collector template. The command sequence downloads and runs a script to generate the support package of the agent.

endpoint_inventory.summary: Get a Site Collector agent uninstallation command
endpoint_inventory.description:
Uninstall command to uninstall the Site Collector agent. The command is encoded in base64, necessitating a decoding step. This encoding ensures the command's integrity during transmission, maintaining its format and preventing alterations. For example, after you receive the response, you can decode the string using the command 
`base64 -d <<< "c3Vkb..............."`
After decoding the command from base64 to its original string format, you'll have the necessary shell commands to uninstall the Site Collector agent. The uninstall command varies depending on the type of Site Collector agent as defined in the Site Collector template. The command sequence downloads and runs a script to delete the agent.

spec_vs_reality_gaps.gap: Spec does not document LOOKUP/IN_TABLE/context_table() syntax nor flag it as unsupported. ALSO: Spec uses 'filter' as the EQL field name; CLAUDE.md documents 'query'. One of the two is wrong — needs investigation.

observed_in_response: record silently dropped when displayName used as key
spec_vs_reality_gaps.gap: Spec documents data items as Map_String (freeform). No mention of opaque attribute IDs vs displayNames. Silent data loss when displayName used as key is undocumented.

observed_in_response: HTTP 404 on US-West (a US-West tenant, confirmed 2026-05-08)
HTTP 200 on SA (an SA tenant, confirmed 2026-05-28)
spec_vs_reality_gaps.gap: Spec documents 404 as a valid error response (resource not found). US-West returned 404 persistently — endpoint was not deployed/routed there. SA returns 200. Regional deployment inconsistency, not a spec defect.

mitre, useCases, tags are ABSENT from both the spec schema and the live response. These fields are UI-only and have never been in the API. Spec is consistent with live behavior. No spec-vs-reality gap. The gap is: there is NO API mechanism to set or read these fields.

observed_in_response: HTTP 500 EXA-INTERNAL-ERROR when sending JSON body
spec_vs_reality_gaps.gap: Spec requires multipart/form-data binary file upload. Our test sent JSON — wrong content type per spec. HTTP 500 instead of 400 for bad content-type is still a server-side defect (should return 415 Unsupported Media Type or 400), but our test was invalid. HTTP 500 is NOT in documented status codes [200, 400, 401, 403, 500].

Per-ID GET endpoint is completely absent from the OpenAPI spec. Spec only documents the list endpoint GET /analytics-rules. HTTP 404 is expected — endpoint was never implemented. This is a missing capability, not a broken endpoint.

Spec documents 4 response fields (timeStartedMillis, timeCompletedMillis, rows, totalRows). Live response has 6 fields — customerQueryId and storageType are undocumented extras. No pagination cursor (nextPage/cursor) documented or present — single-page design. totalRows IS documented, contradicting CLAUDE.md note. CLAUDE.md should be updated: use totalRows not len(rows).

observed_in_response: displayName: null on ALL 109 tables (an SA tenant)
spec_vs_reality_gaps.gap: displayName is NOT in the Table schema in the spec. It is an undocumented field that the live API returns (with null values on an SA tenant). Spec schema: ['id', 'name', 'contextType', 'source', 'attributes', 'attributeMapping', 'totalItems', 'status', 'lastUpdated']. Code that relies on displayName for table lookup has no spec backing — should fall back to name field which IS documented.
